contentHtml.sha256:88a00ce713da9d21589e7a1afdac53a22:
descriptionA visitor checks whether their household can receive pantry food by entering household size and monthly household income, indicating whether someone receives SNAP, and receiving an Eligible or Not eligible result with the applied monthly limit; income at or below the size-based TEFAP limit qualifies, SNAP qualifies regardless of income, and the limit increases by $876 per additional member above eight, while behavior for missing or invalid inputs and required inputs on the SNAP path remains unspecified.
valueHelps households learn whether they qualify for pantry food under the stated income and SNAP rules.
risk: highvisitor
  • The page shows Household size, Monthly household income ($), and Someone in the household receives SNAP inputs, a Check eligibility button, and a result below the button.
  • Households qualify when monthly income is at or below the monthly limit for their size.
  • TEFAP monthly limits effective July 1, 2026, at 185% of poverty are: size 1 $2,461; 2 $3,337; 3 $4,212; 4 $5,088; 5 $5,964; 6 $6,839; 7 $7,715; 8 $8,591; add $876 for each member above 8.
  • A household with someone receiving SNAP is eligible regardless of income.
  • The result states either “Eligible.” or “Not eligible.” and the applied monthly limit.

# SNAP household qualifies despite above-limit income

> For a one-person household with monthly income $2,462 and someone receiving SNAP, eligibility is positive despite exceeding the $2,461 limit, and the applied limit is reported.

## Step 1 @verifies ac-6, ac-7, ac-8, ac-9

At {{start_url}}, open the “Food pantry eligibility check” page, then assert it has an input labelled “Household size”, an input labelled “Monthly household income ($)”, a checkbox labelled “Someone in the household receives SNAP”, and a “Check eligibility” button.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-1, ac-4, ac-5

On the “Food pantry eligibility check” page, set Household size to 1 and Monthly household income ($) to 2462, select “Someone in the household receives SNAP”, and request “Check eligibility”; then assert the result below the button says “Eligible.” and states the applied monthly limit of $2,461.

# Nine-person household qualifies at $9,467

> For a nine-person household without SNAP and monthly income $9,467, the additional-member rule yields an applied limit of $9,467 and eligibility at equality.

## Step 1 @verifies ac-6, ac-7, ac-8, ac-9

At {{start_url}}, open the “Food pantry eligibility check” page, then assert it has an input labelled “Household size”, an input labelled “Monthly household income ($)”, a checkbox labelled “Someone in the household receives SNAP”, and a “Check eligibility” button.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-2, ac-4, ac-5

On the “Food pantry eligibility check” page, set Household size to 9 and Monthly household income ($) to 9467, leave “Someone in the household receives SNAP” unselected, and request “Check eligibility”; then assert the result below the button says “Eligible.” and states the applied monthly limit of $9,467.

# Non-SNAP household above $2,461 is not eligible

> For a one-person household without SNAP earning $2,462 monthly, the result excludes eligibility and reports the $2,461 limit.

## Step 1 @verifies ac-6, ac-7, ac-8, ac-9

At {{start_url}}, open the “Food pantry eligibility check” page, then assert it has an input labelled “Household size”, an input labelled “Monthly household income ($)”, a checkbox labelled “Someone in the household receives SNAP”, and a “Check eligibility” button.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-3, ac-4, ac-5

On the “Food pantry eligibility check” page, set Household size to 1 and Monthly household income ($) to 2462, leave “Someone in the household receives SNAP” unselected, and request “Check eligibility”; then assert the result below the button says “Not eligible.” and states the applied monthly limit of $2,461.
